element.requirements: Allows systems to prompt for performance of planned activities, and validate plans against best practice.
element.short: Action to occur or has occurred as part of plan

binding.description: Identifies the results of the activity.

element.comment: The activity performed is independent of the outcome of the related goal(s). For example, if the goal is to achieve a target body weight of 150 lbs and an activity is defined to exercise, then the activity performed could be amount and intensity of exercise performed whereas the goal outcome is an observation for the actual body weight measured.
element.definition: Identifies the activity that was performed. For example, an activity could be patient education, exercise, or a medication administration. The reference to an "event" resource, such as Procedure or Encounter or Observation, represents the activity that was performed. The requested activity can be conveyed using the CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityReference (a reference to a “request” resource).

mapping.map: {Event that is outcome of Request in activity.plannedActivityReference}

element.requirements: Links plan to resulting actions.
element.short: Activities that are completed or in progress (concept, or Appointment, Encounter, Procedure, etc.)

element.comment: This element should NOT be used to describe the activity to be performed - that occurs within the resource pointed to by CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityReference.
element.definition: Notes about the adherence/status/progress of the activity.
element.requirements: Can be used to capture information about adherence, progress, concerns, etc.

element.comment:
Standard extension exists ([Resource Pertains To Goal](https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/fhir-extensions/StructureDefinition-resource-pertainsToGoal.html)) that allows goals to be referenced from any of the referenced resources in CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityReference.  
The goal should be visible when the resource referenced by CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityReference is viewed independently from the CarePlan.  Requests that are pointed to by a CarePlan using this element should *not* point to this CarePlan using the "basedOn" element.  i.e. Requests that are part of a CarePlan are not "based on" the CarePlan.
element.definition: The details of the proposed activity represented in a specific resource.

mapping.map: {Request that resulted in Event in activity.performedActivity}

element.requirements: Details in a form consistent with other applications and contexts of use.
element.short: Activity that is intended to be part of the care plan

element.definition: General notes about the care plan not covered elsewhere.
element.requirements: Used to capture information that applies to the plan as a whole that doesn't fit into discrete elements.

resource.description: The Care Team includes all the people, organizations, and care teams who participate or plan to participate in the coordination and delivery of care.

element.definition: The Care Team includes all the people, organizations, and care teams who participate or plan to participate in the coordination and delivery of care.
element.short: Planned participants in the coordination and delivery of care

element.comment: This is a business identifier, not a resource identifier (see [discussion](resource.html#identifiers)).  It is best practice for the identifier to only appear on a single resource instance, however business practices may occasionally dictate that multiple resource instances with the same identifier can exist - possibly even with different resource types.  For example, multiple Patient and a Person resource instance might share the same social insurance number.
element.definition: Business identifiers assigned to this care team by the performer or other systems which remain constant as the resource is updated and propagates from server to server.
element.requirements: Allows identification of the care team as it is known by various participating systems and in a way that remains consistent across servers.

binding.description: Indicates the status of the care team.

element.comment: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains the code entered-in-error that marks the care team as not currently valid.
element.definition: Indicates the current state of the care team.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

binding.description: Indicates the type of care team.

element.comment: There may be multiple axis of categorization and one team may serve multiple purposes.
element.definition: Identifies what kind of team.  This is to support differentiation between multiple co-existing teams, such as care plan team, episode of care team, longitudinal care team.
element.requirements: Used for filtering what teams(s) are retrieved and displayed to different types of users.

element.comment: The meaning/purpose of the team is conveyed in CareTeam.category.  This element may also convey semantics of the team (e.g. "Red trauma team"), but its primary purpose is to distinguish between identical teams in a human-friendly way.  ("Team 18735" isn't as friendly.).
element.definition: A label for human use intended to distinguish like teams.  E.g. the "red" vs. "green" trauma teams.
element.short: Name of the team, such as crisis assessment team

element.comment: Use Group for care provision to all members of the group (e.g. group therapy).  Use Patient for care provision to an individual patient.
element.definition: Identifies the patient or group whose intended care is handled by the team.
element.requirements:
Allows the team to care for a group (e.g. marriage) therapy. 
Allows for an organization to designate a team such as the PICC line team.

element.definition: Indicates when the team did (or is intended to) come into effect and end.
element.requirements: Allows tracking what team(s) are in effect at a particular time.

constraint.human: CareTeam.participant.role or CareTeam.participant.member exists

element.definition: Identifies all people and organizations who are expected to be involved in the care team.

mapping.map: REL (REL.4 is always the Patient) ( or PRT?)

binding.description: Indicates specific responsibility of an individual within the care team, such as "Primary physician", "Team coordinator", "Caregiver", etc.

element.comment: Roles may sometimes be inferred by type of Practitioner.  These are relationships that hold only within the context of the care team.  General relationships should be handled as properties of the Patient resource directly.  If a participant has multiple roles within the team, then there should be multiple participants.
element.definition: Indicates specific responsibility of an individual within the care team, such as "Primary care physician", "Trained social worker counselor", "Caregiver", etc.

element.comment:
Patient only needs to be listed if they have a role other than "subject of care".

Member is optional because some participants may be known only by their role, particularly in draft plans. Using Group is only allowed when the group represents a family or a household and should not represent groups of Practitioners.
element.definition: The specific person or organization who is participating/expected to participate in the care team.

mapping.map: REL.5 (or PRT-5 : ( PRV-4 {provider participations} ) / PRT-5 : ( PRV-4  {non-provider person participations} ) / PRT-5 : ( PRV-4 = (patient non-subject of care) ) / PRT-8?)

element.comment: Using Group is only allowed when the group represents a family or a household and should not represent groups of Practitioners.
element.definition: Entity that the participant is acting as a proxy of, or an agent of, or in the interest of, or as a representative of.
element.requirements: Allows specifying which organization a practitioner is acting on behalf of in context of this care team when practitioners are associated with multiple organizations.
element.short: Entity that the participant is acting as a proxy of, or an agent of, or in the interest of, or as a representative of

element.comment: This is populated while creating / managing the CareTeam to ensure there is coverage when servicing CarePlan activities from the Schedule.
element.definition: When the member is generally available within this care team.
element.requirements: To manage members who share the same role, but with different timing.  For example, two physical therapists where one is available Monday through Friday whereas the other is available on the weekend.
element.short: When the member is generally available within this care team

element.comment: Enables care providers a more efficient path to review the participation, if necessary.
element.definition: The basis for the member's role participation in care team.  For example, supporting documentation that establishes legal power of attorney or court ordered guardianship.

binding.description: Indicates the reason for the care team.

element.definition: Describes why the care team exists.
The organization responsible for the care team.
element.requirements: Allows for multiple organizations to collaboratively manage cross-organizational, longitudinal care plan.
element.short: Organization responsible for the care team

element.comment: The ContactPoint.use code of home is not appropriate to use. These contacts are not the contact details of individual care team members.
element.definition: A central contact detail for the care team (that applies to all members).
element.short: A contact detail for the care team (that applies to all members)

element.definition: Comments made about the CareTeam.

resource.description: A provider issued list of professional services and products which have been provided, or are to be provided, to a patient which is sent to an insurer for reimbursement.

element.comment: The Claim resource fulfills three information request requirements: Claim - a request for adjudication for reimbursement for products and/or services provided; Preauthorization - a request to authorize the future provision of products and/or services including an anticipated adjudication; and, Predetermination - a request for a non-bind adjudication of possible future products and/or services.

constraint.human: One and only one .insurance entry may have focal=true.

element.definition: A provider issued list of professional services and products which have been provided, or are to be provided, to a patient which is sent to an insurer for reimbursement.
A unique identifier assigned to this claim.
element.requirements: Allows claims to be distinguished and referenced.

element.definition: Trace number for tracking purposes. May be defined at the jurisdiction level or between trading partners.
element.requirements: Allows partners to uniquely identify components for tracking.

binding.description: A code specifying the state of the resource instance.

element.comment: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains codes that mark the resource as not currently valid.
element.definition: The status of the resource instance.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid
element.requirements: Need to track the status of the resource as 'draft' resources may undergo further edits while 'active' resources are immutable and may only have their status changed to 'cancelled'.

element.comment: Implementation guides may consider adding invariants such that if status = cancelled, statusReason SHALL be supplied.
element.definition: Used to indicate why the status has changed.
element.requirements: This is used to implement conformance on other elements.

binding.description: The type or discipline-style of the claim.

element.comment: The code system provides oral, pharmacy, vision, professional and institutional claim types. Those supported depends on the requirements of the jurisdiction. The valueset is extensible to accommodate other types of claims as required by the jurisdiction.
element.definition: The category of claim, e.g. oral, pharmacy, vision, institutional, professional.
element.requirements: Claim type determine the general sets of business rules applied for information requirements and adjudication.

binding.description: A more granular claim typecode.

element.comment: This may contain the local bill type codes, for example the US UB-04 bill type code or the CMS bill type.
element.definition: A finer grained suite of claim type codes which may convey additional information such as Inpatient vs Outpatient and/or a specialty service.
element.requirements: Some jurisdictions need a finer grained claim type for routing and adjudication.

binding.description: The purpose of the Claim: predetermination, preauthorization, claim.

element.definition: A code to indicate whether the nature of the request is: Claim - A request to an Insurer to adjudicate the supplied charges for health care goods and services under the identified policy and to pay the determined Benefit amount, if any; Preauthorization - A request to an Insurer to adjudicate the supplied proposed future charges for health care goods and services under the identified policy and to approve the services and provide the expected benefit amounts and potentially to reserve funds to pay the benefits when Claims for the indicated services are later submitted; or, Pre-determination - A request to an Insurer to adjudicate the supplied 'what if' charges for health care goods and services under the identified policy and report back what the Benefit payable would be had the services actually been provided.
element.requirements: This element is required to understand the nature of the request for adjudication.

element.definition: The party/group to whom the professional services and/or products have been supplied or are being considered and for whom actual or forecast reimbursement is sought.
element.requirements: The patient must be supplied to the insurer so that confirmation of coverage and service history may be considered as part of the authorization and/or adjudiction.
element.short: The recipient(s) of the products and services

element.comment: Typically this would be today or in the past for a claim, and today or in the future for preauthorizations and predeterminations. Typically line item dates of service should fall within the billing period if one is specified.
element.definition: The period for which charges are being submitted.
element.requirements: A number jurisdictions required the submission of the billing period when submitting claims for example for hospital stays or long-term care.
element.short: Relevant time frame for the claim

element.comment: This field is independent of the date of creation of the resource as it may reflect the creation date of a source document prior to digitization. Typically for claims all services must be completed as of this date.
element.definition: The date this resource was created.
element.requirements: Need to record a timestamp for use by both the recipient and the issuer.

element.definition: Individual who created the claim, predetermination or preauthorization.
element.requirements: Some jurisdictions require the contact information for personnel completing claims.

element.definition: The Insurer who is target of the request.

element.comment: Typically this field would be 1..1 where this party is accountable for the data content within the claim but is not necessarily the facility, provider group or practitioner who provided the products and services listed within this claim resource. This field is the Billing Provider, for example, a facility, provider group, lab or practitioner.
element.definition: The provider which is responsible for the claim, predetermination or preauthorization.

binding.description: The timeliness with which processing is required: stat, normal, deferred.

element.comment: If a claim processor is unable to complete the processing as per the priority then they should generate an error and not process the request.
element.definition: The provider-required urgency of processing the request. Typical values include: stat, normal, deferred.
element.requirements: The provider may need to indicate their processing requirements so that the processor can indicate if they are unable to comply.

binding.description: For whom funds are to be reserved: (Patient, Provider, None).

element.comment: This field is only used for preauthorizations.
element.definition: A code to indicate whether and for whom funds are to be reserved for future claims.
element.requirements: In the case of a Pre-Determination/Pre-Authorization the provider may request that funds in the amount of the expected Benefit be reserved ('Patient' or 'Provider') to pay for the Benefits determined on the subsequent claim(s). 'None' explicitly indicates no funds reserving is requested.

element.comment: For example,  for the original treatment and follow-up exams.
element.definition: Other claims which are related to this claim such as prior submissions or claims for related services or for the same event.
element.requirements: For workplace or other accidents it is common to relate separate claims arising from the same event.

element.definition: Reference to a related claim.
element.requirements: For workplace or other accidents it is common to relate separate claims arising from the same event.

binding.description: Relationship of this claim to a related Claim.

element.comment: For example, prior claim or umbrella.
element.definition: A code to convey how the claims are related.
element.requirements: Some insurers need a declaration of the type of relationship.
element.short: How the reference claim is related

element.comment: For example, Property/Casualty insurer claim # or Workers Compensation case # .
element.definition: An alternate organizational reference to the case or file to which this particular claim pertains.
element.requirements: In cases where an event-triggered claim is being submitted to an insurer which requires a reference number to be specified on all exchanges.

element.definition: Request is the document/authorization given to the claim author for them to provide products and services for which consideration (reimbursement) is sought. Could be a RX for medications, an 'order' for oxygen or wheelchair or physiotherapy treatments.
element.requirements: Required to authorize the dispensing of controlled substances and devices.

element.comment: For example, a physician may prescribe a medication which the pharmacy determines is contraindicated, or for which the patient has an intolerance, and therefore issues a new prescription for an alternate medication which has the same therapeutic intent. The prescription from the pharmacy becomes the 'prescription' and that from the physician becomes the 'original prescription'.
element.definition: Original prescription which has been superseded by this prescription to support the dispensing of pharmacy services, medications or products.
element.requirements: Often required when a fulfiller varies what is fulfilled from that authorized on the original prescription.
element.short: Original prescription if superseded by fulfiller

element.comment: Often billing providers agree to receive the benefits payable to reduce the near-term costs to the patient. The insurer may decline to pay the provider and choose to pay the subscriber instead.
element.definition: The party to be reimbursed for cost of the products and services according to the terms of the policy.
element.requirements: The billing provider needs to specify who they wish to be reimbursed and the claims processor needs express who they will reimburse.

binding.description: A code for the party to be reimbursed.

element.definition: Type of Party to be reimbursed: subscriber, provider, other.
element.requirements: Need to know who should receive payment with the most common situations being the billing Provider (assignment of benefits) or the Subscriber.

element.comment: Not required if the payee is 'subscriber' or 'provider'.
element.definition: Reference to the individual or organization to whom any payment will be made.
element.requirements: Need to provide demographics if the payee is not 'subscriber' nor 'provider'.

element.comment: The referral resource which lists the date, practitioner, reason and other supporting information.
element.definition: The referral information received by the claim author, it is not to be used when the author generates a referral for a patient. A copy of that referral may be provided as supporting information. Some insurers require proof of referral to pay for services or to pay specialist rates for services.
element.requirements: Some insurers require proof of referral to pay for services or to pay specialist rates for services.

element.comment: This will typically be the encounter the event occurred within, but some activities may be initiated prior to or after the official completion of an encounter but still be tied to the context of the encounter.
element.definition: Healthcare encounters related to this claim.
element.requirements: Used in some jurisdictions to link clinical events to claim items.
element.short: Encounters associated with the listed treatments

element.definition: Facility where the services were provided.
element.requirements: Insurance adjudication can be dependant on where services were delivered.

element.comment: For example DRG (Diagnosis Related Group) or a bundled billing code. A patient may have a diagnosis of a Myocardial Infarction and a DRG for HeartAttack would be assigned. The Claim item (and possible subsequent claims) would refer to the DRG for those line items that were for services related to the heart attack event.
element.definition: A package billing code or bundle code used to group products and services to a particular health condition (such as heart attack) which is based on a predetermined grouping code system.
element.requirements: Required to relate the current diagnosis to a package billing code that is then referenced on the individual claim items which are specific to the health condition covered by the package code.

element.definition: Information code for an event with a corresponding date or period.
A coded event such as when a service is expected or a card printed.
A date or period in the past or future indicating when the event occurred or is expectd to occur.
The members of the team who provided the products and services.
element.requirements: Common to identify the responsible and supporting practitioners.

element.definition: A number to uniquely identify care team entries.
element.requirements: Necessary to maintain the order of the care team and provide a mechanism to link individuals to claim details.

element.definition: Member of the team who provided the product or service.
element.requirements: Often a regulatory requirement to specify the responsible provider.

binding.description: The role codes for the care team members.

element.comment: Role might not be required when there is only a single provider listed.
element.definition: The lead, assisting or supervising practitioner and their discipline if a multidisciplinary team.
element.requirements: When multiple parties are present it is required to distinguish the roles performed by each member.

element.definition: The specialization of the practitioner or provider which is applicable for this service.
element.requirements: Need to specify which specialization a practitioner or provider acting under when delivering the product or service.

alias:
Attachments
Exception Codes
Occurrence Codes
Value codes
element.comment: Often there are multiple jurisdiction specific valuesets which are required.
element.definition: Additional information codes regarding exceptions, special considerations, the condition, situation, prior or concurrent issues.
element.requirements: Typically these information codes are required to support the services rendered or the adjudication of the services rendered.

element.definition: A number to uniquely identify supporting information entries.
element.requirements: Necessary to maintain the order of the supporting information items and provide a mechanism to link to claim details.

binding.description: The valuset used for additional information category codes.

element.comment: This may contain a category for the local bill type codes.
element.definition: The general class of the information supplied: information; exception; accident, employment; onset, etc.
element.requirements: Required to group or associate information items with common characteristics. For example: admission information or prior treatments.

binding.description: The valuset used for additional information subcategory codes.

element.definition: A finer classification within the more general category.
element.requirements: Required to provide more detailed categorization, for example lab-test grouping: blood, tissue etc.
element.short: Finer-grained classification of the supplied information

binding.description: The valuset used for additional information codes.

element.definition: System and code pertaining to the specific information regarding special conditions relating to the setting, treatment or patient  for which care is sought.
element.requirements: Required to identify the kind of additional information.

element.definition: The date when or period to which this information refers.

element.comment: Could be used to provide references to other resources, document. For example could contain a PDF in an Attachment of the Police Report for an Accident.
element.definition: Additional data or information such as resources, documents, images etc. including references to the data or the actual inclusion of the data.
element.requirements: To convey the data content to be provided when the information is more than a simple code or period.

binding.description: Reason codes for the missing teeth.

element.comment: For example: the reason for the additional stay, or why a tooth is  missing.
element.definition: Provides the reason in the situation where a reason code is required in addition to the content.
element.requirements: Needed when the supporting information has both a date and amount/value and requires explanation.

element.definition: Information about diagnoses relevant to the claim items.
element.requirements: Required for the adjudication by provided context for the services and product listed.

element.comment: Diagnosis are presented in list order to their expected importance: primary, secondary, etc.
element.definition: A number to uniquely identify diagnosis entries.
element.requirements: Necessary to maintain the order of the diagnosis items and provide a mechanism to link to claim details.

binding.description: Example ICD10 Diagnostic codes.

constraint.human: Either a concept or a reference is provided but not both.

element.definition: The nature of illness or problem in a coded form or as a reference to an external defined Condition.
element.requirements: Provides health context for the evaluation of the products and/or services.

binding.description: The type of the diagnosis: admitting, principal, discharge.

element.comment: For example: admitting, primary, secondary, discharge.
element.definition: When the condition was observed or the relative ranking.
element.requirements: Often required to capture a particular diagnosis, for example: primary or discharge.
element.short: Timing or nature of the diagnosis

binding.description: Present on admission.

element.definition: Indication of whether the diagnosis was present on admission to a facility.
element.requirements: Many systems need to understand for adjudication if the diagnosis was present a time of admission.

element.definition: Procedures performed on the patient relevant to the billing items with the claim.
element.requirements: The specific clinical invention are sometimes required to be provided to justify billing a greater than customary amount for a service.

element.definition: A number to uniquely identify procedure entries.
element.requirements: Necessary to provide a mechanism to link to claim details.

binding.description: Example procedure type codes.

element.comment: For example: primary, secondary.
element.definition: When the condition was observed or the relative ranking.
element.requirements: Often required to capture a particular diagnosis, for example: primary or discharge.

element.definition: Date and optionally time the procedure was performed.
element.requirements: Required for auditing purposes.

binding.description: Example ICD10 Procedure codes.

constraint.human: Either a concept or a reference is provided but not both.

element.definition: The code or reference to a Procedure resource which identifies the clinical intervention performed.
element.requirements: This identifies the actual clinical procedure.

element.definition: Unique Device Identifiers associated with this line item.
element.requirements: The UDI code allows the insurer to obtain device level information on the product supplied.

element.comment: All insurance coverages for the patient which may be applicable for reimbursement, of the products and services listed in the claim, are typically provided in the claim to allow insurers to confirm the ordering of the insurance coverages relative to local 'coordination of benefit' rules. One coverage (and only one) with 'focal=true' is to be used in the adjudication of this claim. Coverages appearing before the focal Coverage in the list, and where 'Coverage.subrogation=false', should provide a reference to the ClaimResponse containing the adjudication results of the prior claim.
element.definition: Financial instruments for reimbursement for the health care products and services specified on the claim.
element.requirements: At least one insurer is required for a claim to be a claim.

element.definition: A number to uniquely identify insurance entries and provide a sequence of coverages to convey coordination of benefit order.
element.requirements: To maintain order of the coverages.

element.comment: A patient may (will) have multiple insurance policies which provide reimbursement for healthcare services and products. For example a person may also be covered by their spouse's policy and both appear in the list (and may be from the same insurer). This flag will be set to true for only one of the listed policies and that policy will be used for adjudicating this claim. Other claims would be created to request adjudication against the other listed policies.
element.definition: A flag to indicate that this Coverage is to be used for adjudication of this claim when set to true.
element.requirements: To identify which coverage in the list is being used to adjudicate this claim.
element.short: Coverage to be used for adjudication

element.comment: Only required in jurisdictions where insurers, rather than the provider, are required to send claims to  insurers that appear after them in the list. This element is not required when 'subrogation=true'.
element.definition: The business identifier to be used when the claim is sent for adjudication against this insurance policy.
element.requirements: This will be the claim number should it be necessary to create this claim in the future. This is provided so that payers may forward claims to other payers in the Coordination of Benefit for adjudication rather than the provider being required to initiate each adjudication.

element.definition: Reference to the insurance card level information contained in the Coverage resource. The coverage issuing insurer will use these details to locate the patient's actual coverage within the insurer's information system.
element.requirements: Required to allow the adjudicator to locate the correct policy and history within their information system.

element.definition: A business agreement number established between the provider and the insurer for special business processing purposes.
element.requirements: Providers may have multiple business arrangements with a given insurer and must supply the specific contract number for adjudication.

element.comment: This value is an alphanumeric string that may be provided over the phone, via text, via paper, or within a ClaimResponse resource and is not a FHIR Identifier.
element.definition: Reference numbers previously provided by the insurer to the provider to be quoted on subsequent claims containing services or products related to the prior authorization.
element.requirements: Providers must quote previously issued authorization reference numbers in order to obtain adjudication as previously advised on the Preauthorization.

element.comment: Must not be specified when 'focal=true' for this insurance.
element.definition: The result of the adjudication of the line items for the Coverage specified in this insurance.
element.requirements: An insurer need the adjudication results from prior insurers to determine the outstanding balance remaining by item for the items in the curent claim.

element.definition: Details of an accident which resulted in injuries which required the products and services listed in the claim.
element.requirements: When healthcare products and services are accident related, benefits may be payable under accident provisions of policies, such as automotive, etc before they are payable under normal health insurance.

element.comment: The date of the accident has to precede the dates of the products and services but within a reasonable timeframe.
element.definition: Date of an accident event  related to the products and services contained in the claim.
element.requirements: Required for audit purposes and adjudication.

binding.description: Type of accident: work place, auto, etc.

element.definition: The type or context of the accident event for the purposes of selection of potential insurance coverages and determination of coordination between insurers.
element.requirements: Coverage may be dependant on the type of accident.

element.definition: The physical location of the accident event.
element.requirements: Required for audit purposes and determination of applicable insurance liability.

element.definition: The amount paid by the patient, in total at the claim claim level or specifically for the item and detail level, to the provider for goods and services.
element.requirements: Necessary to demonstrate that copayments, co-insurance and similar patient payments have been made or accounted for.

element.definition: A claim line. Either a simple  product or service or a 'group' of details which can each be a simple items or groups of sub-details.
element.requirements: The items to be processed for adjudication.

element.definition: A number to uniquely identify item entries.
element.requirements: Necessary to provide a mechanism to link to items from within the claim and within the adjudication details of the ClaimResponse.

element.definition: Trace number for tracking purposes. May be defined at the jurisdiction level or between trading partners.
element.requirements: Allows partners to uniquely identify components for tracking.

element.comment: Profilers should consider making this element required when the backbone .subject is a group.
element.definition: The party to whom the professional services and/or products have been supplied or are being considered and for whom actual for facast reimbursement is sought.
element.short: The recipient of the products and services

element.definition: CareTeam members related to this service or product.
element.requirements: Need to identify the individuals and their roles in the provision of the product or service.

element.definition: Diagnosis applicable for this service or product.
element.requirements: Need to related the product or service to the associated diagnoses.

element.definition: Procedures applicable for this service or product.
element.requirements: Need to provide any listed specific procedures to support the product or service being claimed.

element.definition: Exceptions, special conditions and supporting information applicable for this service or product.
element.requirements: Need to reference the supporting information items that relate directly to this product or service.

binding.description: Codes for the revenue or cost centers supplying the service and/or products.

element.definition: The type of revenue or cost center providing the product and/or service.
element.requirements: Needed in the processing of institutional claims.

binding.description: Benefit categories such as: oral-basic, major, glasses.

element.comment: Examples include Medical Care, Periodontics, Renal Dialysis, Vision Coverage.
element.definition: Code to identify the general type of benefits under which products and services are provided.
element.requirements: Needed in the processing of institutional claims as this allows the insurer to determine whether a facial X-Ray is for dental, orthopedic, or facial surgery purposes.

binding.description: Allowable service and product codes.

element.comment: If this is an actual service or product line, i.e. not a Group, then use code to indicate the Professional Service or Product supplied (e.g. CTP, HCPCS, USCLS, ICD10, NCPDP, DIN, RxNorm, ACHI, CCI). If a grouping item then use a group code to indicate the type of thing being grouped e.g. 'glasses' or 'compound'.
element.definition: When the value is a group code then this item collects a set of related item details, otherwise this contains the product, service, drug or other billing code for the item. This element may be the start of a range of .productOrService codes used in conjunction with .productOrServiceEnd or it may be a solo element where .productOrServiceEnd is not used.
element.requirements: Necessary to state what was provided or done.
element.short: Billing, service, product, or drug code

alias: End of a range of Drug Code; Bill Code; Service Code
element.definition: This contains the end of a range of product, service, drug or other billing codes for the item. This element is not used when the .productOrService is a group code. This value may only be present when a .productOfService code has been provided to convey the start of the range. Typically this value may be used only with preauthorizations and not with claims.
element.short: End of a range of codes

element.definition: Request or Referral for Goods or Service to be rendered.
element.requirements: May identify the service to be provided or provider authorization for the service.

binding.description: Item type or modifiers codes, eg for Oral whether the treatment is cosmetic or associated with TMJ, or an appliance was lost or stolen.

element.comment: For example in Oral whether the treatment is cosmetic or associated with TMJ, or for Medical whether the treatment was outside the clinic or outside of office hours.
element.definition: Item typification or modifiers codes to convey additional context for the product or service.
element.requirements: To support inclusion of the item for adjudication or to charge an elevated fee.

binding.description: Program specific reason codes.

element.comment: For example: Neonatal program, child dental program or drug users recovery program.
element.definition: Identifies the program under which this may be recovered.
element.requirements: Commonly used in in the identification of publicly provided program focused on population segments or disease classifications.
element.short: Program the product or service is provided under

element.definition: The date or dates when the service or product was supplied, performed or completed.
element.requirements: Needed to determine whether the  service or product was provided during the term of the insurance coverage.
element.short: Date or dates of service or product delivery

binding.description: Place of service: pharmacy, school, prison, etc.

element.definition: Where the product or service was provided.
element.requirements: The location can alter whether the item was acceptable for insurance purposes or impact the determination of the benefit amount.
element.short: Place of service or where product was supplied

element.definition: The amount paid by the patient, in total at the claim claim level or specifically for the item and detail level, to the provider for goods and services.
element.requirements: Necessary to demonstrate that copayments, co-insurance and similar patient payments have been made or accounted for.

element.definition: The number of repetitions of a service or product.
element.requirements: Required when the product or service code does not convey the quantity provided.

element.definition: If the item is not a group then this is the fee for the product or service, otherwise this is the total of the fees for the details of the group.
element.requirements: The amount charged to the patient by the provider for a single unit.

resource.name: Claim
resource.purpose: The Claim resource is used by providers to exchange services and products rendered to patients or planned to be rendered with insurers for reimbuserment. It is also used by insurers to exchange claims information with statutory reporting and data analytics firms.

element.comment: The Claim resource fulfills three information request requirements: Claim - a request for adjudication for reimbursement for products and/or services provided; Preauthorization - a request to authorize the future provision of products and/or services including an anticipated adjudication; and, Predetermination - a request for a non-bind adjudication of possible future products and/or services.

resource.description: This resource provides the adjudication details from the processing of a Claim resource.

element.definition: This resource provides the adjudication details from the processing of a Claim resource.
element.short: Response to a claim predetermination or preauthorization

element.definition: A unique identifier assigned to this claim response.
element.requirements: Allows claim responses to be distinguished and referenced.
element.short: Business Identifier for a claim response

element.definition: Trace number for tracking purposes. May be defined at the jurisdiction level or between trading partners.
element.requirements: Allows partners to uniquely identify components for tracking.

binding.description: A code specifying the state of the resource instance.

element.comment: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains codes that mark the resource as not currently valid.
element.definition: The status of the resource instance.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid
element.requirements: Need to track the status of the resource as 'draft' resources may undergo further edits while 'active' resources are immutable and may only have their status changed to 'cancelled'.

element.comment: Implementation guides may consider adding invariants such that if status = cancelled, statusReason SHALL be supplied.
element.definition: Used to indicate why the status has changed.
element.requirements: This is used to implement conformance on other elements.

binding.description: The type or discipline-style of the claim.

element.comment: This may contain the local bill type codes, for example the US UB-04 bill type code or the CMS bill type.
element.definition: A finer grained suite of claim type codes which may convey additional information such as Inpatient vs Outpatient and/or a specialty service.
element.requirements: Some jurisdictions need a finer grained claim type for routing and adjudication.

binding.description: A more granular claim typecode.

element.comment: This may contain the local bill type codes, for example the US UB-04 bill type code or the CMS bill type.
element.definition: A finer grained suite of claim type codes which may convey additional information such as Inpatient vs Outpatient and/or a specialty service.
element.requirements: Some jurisdictions need a finer grained claim type for routing and adjudication.

binding.description: Claim, preauthorization, predetermination.

element.definition: A code to indicate whether the nature of the request is: Claim - A request to an Insurer to adjudicate the supplied charges for health care goods and services under the identified policy and to pay the determined Benefit amount, if any; Preauthorization - A request to an Insurer to adjudicate the supplied proposed future charges for health care goods and services under the identified policy and to approve the services and provide the expected benefit amounts and potentially to reserve funds to pay the benefits when Claims for the indicated services are later submitted; or, Pre-determination - A request to an Insurer to adjudicate the supplied 'what if' charges for health care goods and services under the identified policy and report back what the Benefit payable would be had the services actually been provided.
element.requirements: This element is required to understand the nature of the request for adjudication.

element.definition: The party/group to whom the professional services and/or products have been supplied or are being considered and for whom actual for facast reimbursement is sought.
element.requirements: The patient must be supplied to the insurer so that confirmation of coverage and service hstory may be considered as part of the authorization and/or adjudiction.
element.short: The recipient(s) of the products and services

element.definition: The date this resource was created.
element.requirements: Need to record a timestamp for use by both the recipient and the issuer.

element.definition: The party responsible for authorization, adjudication and reimbursement.
element.requirements: To be a valid claim, preauthorization or predetermination there must be a party who is responsible for adjudicating the contents against a policy which provides benefits for the patient.

element.comment: Typically this field would be 1..1 where this party is accountable for the data content within the claim but is not necessarily the facility, provider group or practitioner who provided the products and services listed within this claim resource. This field is the Billing Provider, for example, a facility, provider group, lab or practitioner..
element.definition: The provider which is responsible for the claim, predetermination or preauthorization.
Original request resource reference.

binding.description: The result of the claim processing.

element.comment: The resource may be used to indicate that the Claim/Preauthorization/Pre-determination has been received but processing has not begun (queued); that it has been processed and one or more errors have been detected (error); no errors were detected and some of the adjudication processing has been performed (partial); or all of the adjudication processing has completed without errors (complete).
element.definition: The outcome of the claim, predetermination, or preauthorization processing.
element.requirements: To advise the requestor of an overall processing outcome.

binding.description: The overall result of the claim adjudication.

element.comment: The element is used to indicate the current state of the adjudication overall for the claim resource, for example: the request has been held (pended) for adjudication processing, for manual review or other reasons; that it has been processed and will be paid, or the outstanding paid, as submitted (approved); that no amount will be paid (denied); or that some amount between zero and the submitted amount will be paid (partial).
element.definition: The result of the claim, predetermination, or preauthorization adjudication.
element.requirements: To advise the requestor of the result of the adjudication process.

element.definition: A human readable description of the status of the adjudication.
element.requirements: Provided for user display.

element.comment: This value is only present on preauthorization adjudications.
element.definition: Reference from the Insurer which is used in later communications which refers to this adjudication.
element.requirements: On subsequent claims, the insurer may require the provider to quote this value.

element.definition: The time frame during which this authorization is effective.
element.requirements: To convey to the provider when the authorized products and services must be supplied for the authorized adjudication to apply.

element.definition: Information code for an event with a corresponding date or period.
A coded event such as when a service is expected or a card printed.
A date or period in the past or future indicating when the event occurred or is expectd to occur.

binding.description: A code for the party to be reimbursed.

element.definition: Type of Party to be reimbursed: subscriber, billing provider, other.
element.requirements: Need to know who should receive payment with the most common situations being the billing Provider (assignment of benefits) or the Subscriber.
element.short: Party to be paid any benefits payable

element.comment: This will typically be the encounter the event occurred within, but some activities may be initiated prior to or after the official completion of an encounter but still be tied to the context of the encounter.
element.definition: Healthcare encounters related to this claim.
element.requirements: Used in some jurisdictions to link clinical events to claim items.
element.short: Encounters associated with the listed treatments

element.comment: For example DRG (Diagnosis Related Group) or a bundled billing code. A patient may have a diagnosis of a Myocardial Infarction and a DRG for HeartAttack would be assigned. The Claim item (and possible subsequent claims) would refer to the DRG for those line items that were for services related to the heart attack event.
element.definition: A package billing code or bundle code used to group products and services to a particular health condition (such as heart attack) which is based on a predetermined grouping code system.
element.requirements: Required to relate the current diagnosis to a package billing code that is then referenced on the individual claim items which are specific to the health condition covered by the package code.

ClinicalUseDefinition NDomainResourceA single issue - either an indication, contraindication, interaction or an undesirable effect for a medicinal product, medication, device or procedure

+ Rule: ClinicalUseDefinition.warning can only be used when type is 'warning'

resource.description: The CodeSystem resource is used to declare the existence of and describe a code system or code system supplement and its key properties, and optionally define a part or all of its content.

constraint.human: Within a code system definition, all the codes SHALL be unique
If there is an explicit hierarchy, a hierarchyMeaning should be provided
If there is an implicit hierarchy, a hierarchyMeaning should be provided
Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation
If the code system content = supplement, it must nominate what it's a supplement for

extension.valueMarkdown: There is scope for unsafe interpretation of codes if it's not known whether the CodeSystem is case sensitive or not

constraint.human: caseSensitive SHOULD be provided

element.definition: The CodeSystem resource is used to declare the existence of and describe a code system or code system supplement and its key properties, and optionally define a part or all of its content.
element.short: Declares the existence of and describes a code system or code system supplement

element.comment:
Can be a urn:uuid: or a urn:oid: but real http: addresses are preferred.  Multiple instances may share the same URL if they have a distinct version.

The determination of when to create a new version of a resource (same url, new version) vs. defining a new artifact is up to the author.  Considerations for making this decision are found in [Technical and Business Versions](resource.html#versions). 

In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the [meta.source](resource.html#meta) element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.

constraint.human: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this code system when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this code system is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the code system is stored on different servers. This is used in [Coding](datatypes.html#Coding).system.
element.requirements: Allows the code system to be referenced by a single globally unique identifier.
element.short: Canonical identifier for this code system, represented as a URI (globally unique) (Coding.system)

element.definition: A formal identifier that is used to identify this code system when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.
element.requirements: Allows externally provided and/or usable business identifiers to be easily associated with the module.
element.short: Additional identifier for the code system (business identifier)

element.comment: There may be different code system instances that have the same identifier but different versions.  The version can be appended to the url in a reference to allow a reference to a particular business version of the code system with the format [url]|[version]. The version SHOULD NOT contain a '#' - see [Business Version](resource.html#bv-format).
element.definition: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the code system when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the code system author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence. This is used in [Coding](datatypes.html#Coding).version.
element.short: Business version of the code system (Coding.version)

element.comment: If set as a string, this is a FHIRPath expression that has two additional context variables passed in - %version1 and %version2 and will return a negative number if version1 is newer, a positive number if version2 and a 0 if the version ordering can't be successfully be determined.
element.definition: Indicates the mechanism used to compare versions to determine which CodeSystem is more current.

element.comment: The name is not expected to be globally unique. The name should be a simple alphanumeric type name to ensure that it is machine-processing friendly.
element.definition: A natural language name identifying the code system. This name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation.
element.requirements: Support human navigation and code generation.
element.short: Name for this code system (computer friendly)

element.comment: This name does not need to be machine-processing friendly and may contain punctuation, white-space, etc.
element.definition: A short, descriptive, user-friendly title for the code system.
element.short: Name for this code system (human friendly)

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

element.comment:
Allows filtering of code systems that are appropriate for use versus not.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.definition: The status of this code system. Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content.
element.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired CodeSystem without due consideration

element.comment:
Allows filtering of code systems that are appropriate for use versus not.. Experimental resources might include example instances in implementation guides, instances created solely for testing purposes, etc. If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource.  (If experimental changes, then it is being misused or a resource that was never intended for real-world use has unexpectedly changed its purpose.).

Experimental resources are not expected to be stable and may well have breaking changes without a corresponding change to the 'version' element.
element.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this code system is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and no version of this resource will ever be intended for genuine usage.
element.meaningWhenMissing: If absent, this resource is treated as though it is not experimental.
element.requirements: Enables experimental content to be developed following the same lifecycle that would be used for a production-level code system.
element.short: For testing only - never for real usage

element.comment:
The date is often not tracked until the resource is published, but may be present on draft content. Note that this is not the same as the resource last-modified-date, since the resource may be a secondary representation of the code system. Additional specific dates may be added as extensions or be found by consulting Provenances associated with past versions of the resource.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.definition: The date  (and optionally time) when the code system was last significantly changed. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the code system changes.

element.comment: Usually an organization but may be an individual. The publisher (or steward) of the code system is the organization or individual primarily responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the code system. This is not necessarily the same individual or organization that developed and initially authored the content. The publisher is the primary point of contact for questions or issues with the code system. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context.
element.definition: The name of the organization or individual responsible for the release and ongoing maintenance of the code system.
element.requirements: Helps establish the "authority/credibility" of the code system.  May also allow for contact.
element.short: Name of the publisher/steward (organization or individual)

element.comment:
May be a web site, an email address, a telephone number, etc.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.definition: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.

element.comment: This description can be used to capture details such as comments about misuse, instructions for clinical use and interpretation, literature references, examples from the paper world, etc. It is not a rendering of the code system as conveyed in the 'text' field of the resource itself. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context (e.g. the language of the code system is presumed to be the predominant language in the place the code system was created).
element.definition: A free text natural language description of the code system from a consumer's perspective.
element.short: Natural language description of the code system

element.comment: When multiple useContexts are specified, there is no expectation that all or any of the contexts apply.
element.definition: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate code system instances.
element.requirements: Assist in searching for appropriate content.
element.short: The context that the content is intended to support

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

element.comment: It may be possible for the code system to be used in jurisdictions other than those for which it was originally designed or intended.
element.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating.  In general, the jurisdiction is also found in the useContext.  The useContext may reference additional jurisdictions because the defining jurisdiction does not necessarily limit the jurisdictions of use.
element.short: Jurisdiction of the authority that maintains the code system (if applicable)

element.comment: This element does not describe the usage of the code system. Instead, it provides traceability of ''why'' the resource is either needed or ''why'' it is defined as it is.  This may be used to point to source materials or specifications that drove the structure of this code system.
element.definition: Explanation of why this code system is needed and why it has been designed as it has.
element.short: Why this code system is defined

element.comment: ... Sometimes, the copyright differs between the code system and the codes that are included. The copyright statement should clearly differentiate between these when required.
element.definition: A copyright statement relating to the code system and/or its contents. Copyright statements are notices of intellectual property ownership and can include restrictions on the use and publishing of the code system.
element.requirements: Consumers must be able to determine any legal restrictions on the use of the code system and/or its content.
element.short: Notice about intellectual property ownership, can include restrictions on use

element.comment: The copyright symbol and the '(c)' textual representation SHOULD NOT be included in this string. It will be added by software when rendering the notation. Full details about licensing, restrictions, warrantees, etc. goes in the more general 'copyright' element.
element.definition: A short string (<50 characters), suitable for inclusion in a page footer that identifies the copyright holder, effective period, and optionally whether rights are restricted. (e.g. 'All rights reserved', 'Some rights reserved').
element.requirements: Defines the content expected to be rendered in all representations of the artifact.

element.comment:
The 'date' element may be more recent than the approval date because of minor changes or editorial corrections.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was approved by the publisher. Approval happens once when the content is officially approved for usage.
element.short: When the CodeSystem was approved by publisher

element.comment:
If specified, this date follows the original approval date.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was last reviewed. Review happens periodically after approval but does not change the original approval date.
element.requirements: Gives a sense of how "current" the content is.  Resources that have not been reviewed in a long time may have a risk of being less appropriate/relevant.
element.short: When the CodeSystem was last reviewed by the publisher

element.comment:
The effective period for a CodeSystem  determines when the content is applicable for usage and is independent of publication and review dates. For example, a system intended to be used for the year 2016 might be published in 2015.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.definition: The period during which the CodeSystem content was or is planned to be in active use.
element.requirements: Allows establishing a transition before a resource comes into effect and also allows for a sunsetting  process when new versions of the CodeSystem are or are expected to be used instead.
element.short: When the CodeSystem is expected to be used

element.definition: Descriptions related to the content of the CodeSystem. Topics provide a high-level categorization as well as keywords for the CodeSystem that can be useful for filtering and searching.
element.requirements: Repositories must be able to determine how to categorize the CodeSystem so that it can be found by topical and keyword searches.

element.definition: An individual or organization primarily involved in the creation and maintenance of the CodeSystem.
An individual or organization primarily responsible for internal coherence of the CodeSystem.

+ Rule: Within a code system definition, all the codes SHALL be unique
+ Warning: If there is an explicit hierarchy, a hierarchyMeaning should be provided

+ Rule: If the code system content = supplement, it must nominate what it's a supplement for

resource.description: A clinical or business level record of information being transmitted or shared; e.g. an alert that was sent to a responsible provider, a public health agency communication to a provider/reporter in response to a case report for a reportable condition.

element.definition: A clinical or business level record of information being transmitted or shared; e.g. an alert that was sent to a responsible provider, a public health agency communication to a provider/reporter in response to a case report for a reportable condition.
element.short: A clinical or business level record of information being transmitted or shared

element.comment: This is a business identifier, not a resource identifier (see [discussion](resource.html#identifiers)).  It is best practice for the identifier to only appear on a single resource instance, however business practices may occasionally dictate that multiple resource instances with the same identifier can exist - possibly even with different resource types.  For example, multiple Patient and a Person resource instance might share the same social insurance number.
element.definition: Business identifiers assigned to this communication by the performer or other systems which remain constant as the resource is updated and propagates from server to server.
element.requirements: Allows identification of the communication as it is known by various participating systems and in a way that remains consistent across servers.

element.definition: An order, proposal or plan fulfilled in whole or in part by this Communication.

element.comment: The event the communication was part of - e.g. if you disclosed as "part" of counselling, it would be partOf that Procedure.
element.definition: A larger event (e.g. Communication, Procedure) of which this particular communication is a component or step.
element.short: Part of referenced event (e.g. Communication, Procedure)

element.definition: Prior communication that this communication is in response to.

binding.description: The status of the communication.

element.comment: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains the codes aborted and entered-in-error that mark the communication as not currently valid.
element.definition: The status of the transmission.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid
element.short: preparation | in-progress | not-done | on-hold | stopped | completed | entered-in-error | unknown

binding.description: Codes for the reason why a communication did not happen.

element.comment: This is generally only used for "exception" statuses such as "not-done", "suspended" or "aborted". The reason for performing the event at all is captured in reasonCode, not here.
element.definition: Captures the reason for the current state of the Communication.

binding.description: Codes for general categories of communications such as alerts, instructions, etc.

element.comment: There may be multiple axes of categorization and one communication may serve multiple purposes.
element.definition: The type of message conveyed such as alert, notification, reminder, instruction, etc.

binding.description: Codes indicating the relative importance of a communication.

element.comment: Used to prioritize workflow (such as which communication to read first) when the communication is planned or in progress.
element.definition: Characterizes how quickly the planned or in progress communication must be addressed. Includes concepts such as stat, urgent, routine.
element.meaningWhenMissing: If missing, this communication should be treated with normal priority

binding.description: Codes for communication mediums such as phone, fax, email, in person, etc.

element.definition: A channel that was used for this communication (e.g. email, fax, SMS).
The patient or group that was the focus of this communication.

binding.description: Codes describing the purpose or content of the communication.

element.comment: Communication.topic.text can be used without any codings.
element.definition: Description of the purpose/content, similar to a subject line in an email.

element.definition: Completed or terminated request(s) whose function is taken by this new request.
element.requirements: Allows tracing the continuation of a therapy or administrative process instantiated through multiple requests.

element.comment: Requests are linked either by a "basedOn" relationship (i.e. one request is fulfilling another) or by having a common requisition.  Requests that are part of the same requisition are generally treated independently from the perspective of changing their state or maintaining them after initial creation.
element.definition: A shared identifier common to multiple independent Request instances that were activated/authorized more or less simultaneously by a single author.  The presence of the same identifier on each request ties those requests together and may have business ramifications in terms of reporting of results, billing, etc.  E.g. a requisition number shared by a set of lab tests ordered together, or a prescription number shared by all meds ordered at one time.

resource.description: Composition provides the structural backbone for assembling a set of healthcare-related information into a single logical package that provides a single coherent statement of meaning, establishes its own context and has traceability to the author who is making the statement.

element.comment: While the focus of this specification is on patient-specific clinical statements, this resource can also apply to other healthcare-related statements such as study protocol designs, healthcare invoices and other activities that are not necessarily patient-specific or clinical.
element.definition: Composition provides the structural backbone for assembling a set of healthcare-related information into a single logical package that provides a single coherent statement of meaning, establishes its own context and has traceability to the author who is making the statement.
element.short: A set of resources composed into a single coherent clinical statement with clinical attestation

element.comment: Can be a urn:uuid: or a urn:oid: but real http: addresses are preferred. Multiple instances may share the same URL if they have a distinct version.
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this Composition when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this Composition is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the Composition is stored on different servers.
element.requirements: Allows the Composition to be referenced by a single globally unique identifier.
element.short: Canonical identifier for this Composition, represented as a URI (globally unique)

element.comment: Similar to ClinicalDocument/setId in CDA. See discussion in resource definition for how these relate.
element.definition: A version-independent identifier for the Composition. This identifier stays constant as the composition is changed over time.

element.comment: This element is the author-assigned business version of the Composition (analogous to CDA ClinicalDocument.versionNumber). It is distinct from Resource.meta.versionId, which is a server-assigned technical version that every resource carries and that may change whenever the resource is updated on a server. Composition.version reflects the version of a logical document's content and remains constant even if the Composition or its referenced resources are moved between servers and receive new meta.versionId values.
element.definition: An explicitly assigned identifier of a variation of the content in the Composition.
element.short: An explicitly assigned identifier of a variation of the content in the Composition

element.definition: References the consents associated with this document. Examples include a consent to perform the clinical service being documented (.event) or a consent for the information contained in the document to be released to a third party.
element.short: Represents informed consents and medico-legal transactions

element.definition: A plan, proposal or order that is fulfilled in whole or in part by this composition.
element.requirements: Allows tracing of authorization for the event and tracking whether proposals/recommendations were acted upon.

binding.description: The workflow status of the composition.

element.comment: See section 2.8.3.2, The workflow/clinical status of the composition, for guidance.  Because the entered-in-error flag changes how this resource and its related elements must be interpreted, status is labeled as a modifier element. Some reporting workflows require that the original narrative of a final document never be altered; instead, only new narrative can be added. The Composition resource has no explicit status for noting whether this business rule is in effect; this would be handled by an extension if required.
element.definition: The workflow/clinical status of this composition. The status is a marker for the clinical standing of the document.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid
